newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks take Iranian hunger strikers to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Turks take Iranian hunger strikers to hospital.

text.p: Turkish police and health officials on Friday forcibly took 15 Iranian asylum seekers to hospital after a hunger strike of 46 days, human rights activists said.

"Police and health officials took them, including three women in very bad condition, to two separete hospitals, despite the fact that they refused treatment," Kamil Atesogullari from the independent Human Rights Association told Reuters.

The hunger strikers were protesting at the refusal by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to send 165 Iranian asylum-seekers in Ankara to third countries, he said. The group, including 60 children and 40 women, have been in Turkey for 15 months, Atesogullari said.
UNHCR officials in Ankara say the Iranians do not qualify for refugee status as they were simply seeking better economic conditions in European countries.
Atesogullari said the interior ministry had told the Iranians they would be deported by October 2 if they could not obtain a visa or passport to go to a third country.
Turkey said this year it had no obligation to non-European refugees but would help them seek asylum in third countries.
